title: B1 · L47 — Social issues (basic)
description: Vocabulario para hablar de asuntos sociales: inequality, education, healthcare, homelessness, poverty, unemployment.

questions.prompt: Situación: lees un artículo sobre desigualdad económica global.
questions.question: What does 'inequality' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Inequality' = desigualdad, diferencias INJUSTAS entre personas/grupos. Se aplica a economía, género, oportunidades, salud. Colocaciones: 'income inequality', 'gender inequality', 'social inequality'. Antónimo: 'equality'. Nota el prefijo 'in-' que invierte el sentido de 'equality'.
examples: Income inequality has been rising steadily since the 1980s. → dato histórico
Gender inequality still exists in many workplaces. → observación laboral

questions.prompt: Defiendes el acceso universal a un servicio básico.
questions.question: Complete: 'Free ___ should be available to everyone.'
questions.explanation: 'Free education' es colocación central en debates sociales — un derecho reconocido en muchas constituciones. 'Car/phone/TV' son bienes, no derechos. Colocaciones asociadas: 'free healthcare', 'free speech', 'free press'. 'Free' aquí = gratuito, no 'libre' (aunque también puede serlo).
examples: Free education is considered a basic right in most democracies. → contexto político
Many European countries offer free education at university level. → dato geográfico

questions.statement: 'Poverty' means the state of being extremely poor.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Poverty' /ˈpɒvəti/ = pobreza. Adjetivo: 'poor'. Categorías: 'extreme poverty' (menos de $2/día), 'relative poverty' (por debajo de la media local). Colocaciones: 'live in poverty', 'fight poverty', 'poverty line' (umbral de pobreza). Objetivo de la ONU: eradicate extreme poverty by 2030.
examples: Millions of people live in extreme poverty worldwide. → dato macro
We need to reduce poverty through education and jobs. → soluciones estructurales

questions.text: Access to good healthcare is one of the most important social issues today.
questions.explanation: Nota 'access' /ˈækses/ con doble 'c' /ks/. 'Healthcare' (una sola palabra) — no 'health care' (dos). 'Social issues' con 'ʃ' suave. Colocaciones B1 clave: 'access to healthcare/education/services'. 'Social issue' = tema que afecta a toda la sociedad, no solo individuos.
examples: Everyone deserves access to healthcare, regardless of income. → argumento moral
Healthcare is considered a basic right in most European countries. → contexto político

questions.prompt: Discutes cómo el estado debería apoyar a las personas sin hogar.
questions.question: Complete: 'The government should do more to help ___ people.'
questions.explanation: 'Homeless' /ˈhəʊmləs/ = sin hogar. 'Homely' (UK) = acogedor, hogareño; (US) = sin gracia física (¡falso amigo peligroso!). 'Homework' es deberes escolares. 'Houseful' no existe. Colocaciones respetuosas: 'homeless people', 'people experiencing homelessness'. Evita términos peyorativos.
examples: There are many homeless people in big cities like London. → contexto urbano
The charity helps homeless people find shelter and jobs. → intervención social

questions.prompt: Empareja cada problema social con su definición:
questions.explanation: Cuatro términos clave para debatir problemas sociales estructurales. Aparecen constantemente en noticias, políticas públicas, ONGs y programas electorales. Distinción B1 clave: 'inequality' es la CAUSA sistémica; 'poverty/unemployment' son EFECTOS observables; 'healthcare' es un SERVICIO/derecho.
examples: Unemployment is high in this region — nearly 15%. → dato regional
Poverty affects many families across generations. → efecto duradero

questions.question: Choose: '___ is when people don't have a job.'
questions.explanation: 'Unemployment' = desempleo. Prefijo 'un-' invierte el sentido de 'employment' (empleo). 'Payment' es pago; 'enjoyment' es disfrute — ambos sufijos '-ment' pero distinto sentido. Colocaciones: 'unemployment rate', 'youth unemployment', 'high/low unemployment'. Se pronuncia /ˌʌnɪmˈplɔɪmənt/.
examples: Unemployment rates are rising in some sectors. → cambio económico
Youth unemployment is a serious problem in many countries. → grupo específico

questions.target: I think education is the best way to solve many social problems in the world.
questions.explanation: Situación: expresas tu opinión en un debate sobre soluciones sociales. Estructura B1 clara: 'I think + X + is the best way to + inf'. 'Many' suaviza — no dice 'all'. Contracción implícita en habla. Tono reflexivo, opinión fundamentada sin ser dogmático. Evita 'The best way' (absoluto).
examples: I believe healthcare is a basic human right that shouldn't depend on income. → argumento moral
I think we should fight inequality at every level — starting locally. → llamada a la acción

questions.statement: 'Discrimination' means treating people unfairly because of their race, gender or beliefs.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Discrimination' /dɪˌskrɪmɪˈneɪʃən/ = trato injusto basado en características personales (raza, género, religión, edad, orientación). Tipos: racial, gender, age, religious discrimination. Colocaciones: 'face/fight/experience discrimination'. Ilegal en muchos contextos según legislaciones nacionales.
examples: Discrimination is illegal in most countries when hiring. → contexto laboral
We should all actively fight against discrimination in our communities. → compromiso cívico

questions.prompt: Hablas de una campaña sobre salud mental.
questions.question: Complete: 'We need to raise ___ about mental health.'
questions.explanation: 'Raise awareness about + tema' = concienciar sobre un tema. Colocación fija de campañas sociales. 'Raise money' funciona pero para recaudar fondos, no concienciar. Colocaciones asociadas: 'raise a family/concern/issue/objection'. 'Awareness' /əˈweənəs/ es sustantivo abstracto de 'aware' (consciente).
examples: Charities raise awareness about many overlooked issues. → labor social
The campaign raised awareness about ocean pollution effectively. → impacto medible

questions.text: Governments should invest more in education to give everyone equal opportunities.
questions.explanation: Nota 'governments' con 'n' apenas audible /ˈɡʌvəmənts/. 'Invest in' con 'in' débil /ɪn/. 'Equal opportunities' con acento en 'e-' de 'equal'. Colocaciones B1 clave: 'invest in education', 'equal opportunities'. Discurso político estándar sobre igualdad de oportunidades — muy usado en programas electorales.
examples: Investing in education is essential for long-term growth. → argumento macro
Equal opportunities benefit everyone in the long run, not just individuals. → visión colectiva

questions.prompt: Distingues qué es un problema social real.
questions.question: Which is a SOCIAL ISSUE?
questions.explanation: 'Poverty' es problema social estructural que afecta a millones. Las otras tres son actividades cotidianas individuales, no problemas colectivos. Regla B1: 'social issue' implica escala colectiva + causa estructural + efecto en calidad de vida. Otros: unemployment, homelessness, inequality.
examples: Poverty affects millions worldwide — even in rich countries. → escala global
Ending poverty is one of the UN's key global goals. → contexto institucional

questions.statement: 'Human rights' are basic rights that every person should have.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Human rights' = derechos fundamentales universales (vida, libertad, seguridad, educación, trabajo digno, no discriminación). Definidos en la Declaración Universal de la ONU (1948). Colocaciones: 'human rights violations', 'human rights activist', 'protect/violate human rights'.
examples: Everyone has human rights, regardless of nationality or status. → principio universal
Human rights must be protected by law and enforced actively. → dimensión institucional

questions.prompt: Describes qué hace una ONG internacional.
questions.question: Complete: 'The organisation ___ children in need around the world.'
questions.explanation: 'Help + persona + in need' = ayudar a personas en situación vulnerable. Colocación fija humanitaria. 'Make/do/take' no forman esta colocación. Estructura: 'help + object + (to) + inf' o 'help + object + with + noun'. Verbo central del discurso solidario.
examples: The charity helps people in need through food banks and shelters. → método concreto
We should all try to help those in need whenever possible. → llamada personal

questions.target: I believe we should all try to help solve important social issues in our community.
questions.explanation: Situación: cierres de discurso motivacional en un evento social o clase de inglés. Estructura B1 potente: 'I believe we should all + inf'. 'Solve social issues' es colocación profesional. 'In our community' aterriza el mensaje (no abstracto). Tono cívico y esperanzador, con contracción implícita en habla.
examples: We should all fight discrimination — starts with small acts. → llamada concreta
Everyone can help their community in some small but real way. → optimismo realista
